**In one line**: OpenAI reportedly told lawmakers in a letter that it is developing "automated shutdown" capabilities that can halt its AI tools when needed.

### Key points
- OpenAI is said to have described building "automated shutdown" capabilities for its AI tools in a letter to U.S. lawmakers.
- The feature is framed as a safety mechanism that would automatically stop an AI system in dangerous or out-of-control situations.
- The letter surfaced through the company's ongoing communication with regulators and legislators, reflecting rising policy attention to AI safety.

### Why it matters
An automatic "off switch" sits at the center of long-running debates over AI controllability. A leading lab presenting such a safeguard in regulatory correspondence signals that AI safety is moving from a purely technical topic into legislative and policy territory.
